chapter_theme: A song at Pugazhimalai (புகழிமலை): the poet fears drowning in the sea of women, possessions, wife and children, and asks Murugan to come on the peacock with the life of the lotus feet.

619.reading: The poet asks whether, through women's fragrant hair, lined eyes, faces and young breasts, through the possessions he thinks of, and through wife and children, he will sink and wander in the waves of the sea; he asks Murugan to come before him on the peacock with compassion and give the life of the lotus feet. The praise names Murugan worshipped by Brahma, Vishnu, gods and sages, lord of the Bhoga land with its rivers and groves, who threw the vel that pierced Sura's mountain and dried the sea, at Pugazhimalai, praised by the Tamil sage.
619.nuance: The list moves from women to wealth (கருது பொருள்) to wife and children (மனைவி மகவு) as one sea, so that household life and courtesans are the same entanglement. தமிழ் முநிவர், the Tamil sage, is probably Agastya.
